subject: Formation personnelle et sociale
bigIdeas: Comprendre et gérer mes émotions pour bien vivre

lessons.title: Qu'est-ce que je ressens?
lessons.goal: Students will identify and name basic emotions (happy, sad, angry, scared) in French
safetyConsiderations: Créer un espace sécuritaire pour partager
Respecter qui ne veut pas partager

opening.description: Introduction to emotions with curiosity and acceptance
activities: Regarder dans le miroir: 'Comment je me sens aujourd'hui?'
Présenter la marionnette qui ressent aussi des émotions
Chanson d'accueil: 'Bonjour mes émotions'

mainActivity.description: Explore basic emotions with safety and acceptance
activities: Découvrir les 4 émotions de base avec cartes visuelles
Marionnette montre chaque émotion (content, triste, fâché, peur)
Jeu 'Montre-moi l'émotion' avec visages
Histoire simple: 'La journée d'émotions de Léa'
Journal des émotions: dessiner comment on se sent
mainActivity.visualSupports: Cartes émotions, marionnette, gestes TPR, livre illustré
mainActivity.movementBreak: Danse des émotions - bouger comme on se sent

closing.description: Celebrate emotions and normalize all feelings
activities: Cercle: partage optionnel 'Je me sens...'
Affiche de classe: 'Toutes les émotions sont OK'
Chanson de fermeture calme
closing.visualSupports: Cercle inclusif, affiche colorée, gestes apaisants

decisionPoints.situation: How comfortable are students talking about feelings?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students seem shy → use marionnette more, model sharing first | IF students are eager → encourage but keep sharing brief

decisionPoints.situation: What visual supports help with emotion vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students need more support → use larger cards, more gestures | IF students are following well → add emotion faces mirror work

decisionPoints.situation: How to create a safe space for sharing?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students seem worried → emphasize 'all emotions are normal' | IF sharing gets intense → redirect to marionnette examples

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus only on 'content' and 'triste' with lots of visual support
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More movement, puppet interaction, and silly faces
emergencyBackup.ifSensitive: Use only puppet sharing, no personal sharing pressure

lessons.realWorldConnection: Knowing how we feel helps us tell parents, teachers, and friends what we need
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe students identifying emotions, listen to vocabulary use
lessons.differentiationSupport: Visual learners: more emotion cards | Kinesthetic: emotion movements | Language: simple gestures and modeling

lessons.title: Mon visage montre mes émotions
lessons.goal: Students will recognize emotions in facial expressions and connect faces to feelings
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 1 by adding visual recognition of emotions through facial expressions
materials: Photos diverses d'enfants montrant des émotions
safetyConsiderations: Utiliser des photos diverses et inclusives
Éviter de forcer les expressions faciales

opening.description: Connect faces to feelings from yesterday
activities: Révision: 'Hier on a appris les émotions'
Miroir: faire un visage content, puis triste
Marionnette montre ses expressions

mainActivity.description: Practice reading faces and making expressions
activities: Explorer photos d'enfants: 'Comment se sent-il/elle?'
Jeu de miroir: copier les expressions
Masques d'émotions: porter et deviner
Histoire: 'Le visage de Thomas change'
Dessiner son propre visage d'émotion préférée
mainActivity.visualSupports: Photos d'enfants, masques, miroirs, histoire illustrée
mainActivity.movementBreak: Jeu 'Statues d'émotions' - figer avec une expression

activities: Regarder les amis: 'Comment se sentent-ils maintenant?'
Partage: 'Mon visage maintenant montre...'
Création d'une galerie de visages heureux
closing.visualSupports: Observation respectueuse, galerie de classe

decisionPoints.situation: Are students connecting faces to emotions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students struggle → use more obvious expressions, more modeling | IF students are good → add subtle expression photos

decisionPoints.situation: What emotion faces are most relatable?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF using diverse photos → discuss how all faces show emotions | IF students relate well → encourage them to share their own

decisionPoints.situation: How to address different cultural expressions of emotion?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF questions arise → 'families show emotions differently' | IF confusion → focus on universal expressions first

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on clear happy/sad faces only with simple pointing
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More mirror play, silly face games
emergencyBackup.ifSensitive: Use cartoon faces instead of real photos if preferred

lessons.realWorldConnection: Reading faces helps us know when friends need help or want to play
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Watch students matching faces to emotions, observe expression making
lessons.differentiationSupport: Visual learners: more photos | Kinesthetic: mirror work | Social: partner face reading

lessons.title: Mon corps ressent aussi
lessons.goal: Students will identify where emotions are felt in the body (heart racing, tight tummy, etc.)
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 2 by exploring how emotions manifest physically in our bodies
safetyConsiderations: Respecter le confort de chacun avec le corps

activities: Rappel: 'Notre visage montre nos émotions'
Question: 'Où sent-on les émotions dans le corps?'
Marionnette touche son cœur: 'J'ai des sentiments ici aussi'
opening.visualSupports: Marionnette, gestes vers le corps, curiosité

mainActivity.description: Explore body sensations connected to emotions
activities: Écouter notre cœur avec stéthoscope (content vs nerveux)
Silhouette: colorier où on sent la joie (cœur jaune)
Silhouette: colorier où on sent la peur (ventre rouge)
Respiration: sentir le ventre qui bouge
Histoire: 'Les émotions de Mia dans son corps'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Silhouette grande, autocollants, stéthoscope, démonstrations
mainActivity.movementBreak: Étirements doux pour relâcher les tensions

activities: Scan corporel: 'Comment se sent mon corps maintenant?'
Dessiner une émotion dans le corps
Respiration calme ensemble
closing.visualSupports: Positions confortables, dessins simples, respiration guidée

decisionPoints.situation: How are students connecting body sensations to emotions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students struggle → use more concrete examples, touch own heart | IF students connect well → explore more body parts

decisionPoints.situation: What body awareness activities work best?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students love stethoscope → more heart listening activities | IF students prefer movement → more emotion stretches

decisionPoints.situation: Are all students comfortable with body talk?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF some students uncomfortable → use marionnette body, keep impersonal | IF all comfortable → personal sharing OK

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus only on heart and happy feelings
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More stethoscope time, silly body movements
emergencyBackup.ifSensitive: Use only marionnette body, no personal body references

lessons.realWorldConnection: When our body tells us we're worried, we can ask for help or take deep breaths
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Listen to body sensation vocabulary, observe body awareness
lessons.differentiationSupport: Tactile learners: stethoscope, cushions | Visual: body diagrams | Kinesthetic: movement breaks

lessons.title: Toutes les émotions sont normales
lessons.goal: Students will understand that all emotions are normal and acceptable to feel
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 3 by normalizing all emotions and reducing emotional shame
safetyConsiderations: Valider toutes les émotions sans jugement

activities: Révision: 'Nos émotions dans notre corps'
Question: 'Y a-t-il des émotions méchantes?'
Marionnette: 'Moi aussi je ressens toutes ces émotions'
Arc-en-ciel des émotions: 'Chaque couleur est belle'
Histoire: 'La famille émotions - tous important'
Boîte magique: mettre toutes les émotions dedans avec amour
Chaque enfant reçoit un cœur: 'Tes émotions sont précieuses'
Création affiche de classe: 'Ici, toutes les émotions sont OK'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Arc-en-ciel coloré, livre inclusif, boîte décorée, cœurs colorés
mainActivity.movementBreak: Danse libre: 'Bouger selon notre émotion du moment'

activities: Cercle: 'Une émotion que j'accepte chez moi'
Promesse de classe: 'Nous acceptons toutes les émotions'
Câlin collectif à l'affiche des émotions
closing.visualSupports: Cercle chaleureux, affiche visible, gestes d'acceptation

decisionPoints.situation: How to validate all emotions without judgment?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students say emotions are 'bad' → redirect with 'uncomfortable but normal' | IF students accept easily → deepen with examples

decisionPoints.situation: What examples resonate with student experiences?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students share personal examples → validate and normalize | IF students seem hesitant → use story characters

decisionPoints.situation: How to address 'bad' vs 'uncomfortable' emotions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students use 'bad' language → teach 'uncomfortable' instead | IF understanding is clear → reinforce with more examples

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'all feelings are OK' with simple examples
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More interactive activities with the emotion box
emergencyBackup.ifSensitive: Extra validation and reassurance about normalcy

lessons.realWorldConnection: When we accept our emotions, we feel better about ourselves and can get help easier
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Listen for acceptance language, observe comfort with emotion talk
lessons.differentiationSupport: Verbal processors: more discussion | Visual: more charts | Emotional: extra validation

lessons.title: Dire mes sentiments
lessons.goal: Students will practice expressing emotions using simple French phrases
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 4 by providing language tools to express accepted emotions
safetyConsiderations: Respecter le rythme de chacun pour parler

activities: Rappel: 'Toutes nos émotions sont normales'
Question: 'Comment dire nos émotions aux autres?'
Marionnette: 'Je vais apprendre à dire mes sentiments'

mainActivity.description: Practice expressing emotions with words and alternatives
activities: Apprendre phrases: 'Je me sens content', 'Je me sens triste'
Téléphones: pratiquer dire ses émotions à un ami
Marionnettes dialogue: modeler l'expression émotionnelle
Tableau de classe: pointer et dire 'Je me sens...'
Jeu 'Devine mon émotion': dire sans gestes
mainActivity.visualSupports: Cartes phrases, téléphones colorés, tableau interactif, marionnettes
mainActivity.movementBreak: Marcher et dire son émotion du moment

activities: Cercle: chacun dit 'Maintenant je me sens...'
Création d'un dictionnaire d'émotions de classe
Chanson: 'Je peux dire mes émotions'
closing.visualSupports: Cercle supportant, livre de classe, chanson simple

decisionPoints.situation: Which phrases are most useful for students?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students master basic → add 'Je me sens un peu...' | IF students struggle → focus on 2 phrases only

decisionPoints.situation: How to encourage shy students to share?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students very shy → offer whisper option or pointing | IF students eager → encourage but manage turns

decisionPoints.situation: What communication methods work beyond verbal?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF verbal challenging → use pointing, gestures, drawing | IF verbal easy → add tone and facial expression

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'content' and 'triste' expressions only
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More telephone play and puppet conversations
emergencyBackup.ifSensitive: Use only puppet expressing, no personal pressure

lessons.realWorldConnection: When we tell people how we feel, they can help us or celebrate with us
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Listen to emotion phrases, observe communication attempts
lessons.differentiationSupport: Verbal learners: more phrase practice | Non-verbal: pointing options | Social: partner practice

lessons.title: Quand je suis content
lessons.goal: Students will explore positive emotions and appropriate ways to express joy
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 5 by focusing specifically on positive emotions and their expression

activities: Rappel: 'On peut dire nos émotions'
Question: 'Qu'est-ce qui nous rend content?'
Marionnette fait une danse de joie
Regarder photos d'enfants heureux: 'Comment montrent-ils la joie?'
Brainstorm: 'Qu'est-ce qui me rend heureux?'
Bulles de joie: attraper et rire ensemble
Danse de la joie avec musique douce
Dessiner 'Mon moment le plus heureux'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Photos joyeuses, bulles magiques, musique entraînante, art supplies
mainActivity.movementBreak: Sautiller de joie (contrôlé et sécuritaire)

activities: Partage: 'Quelque chose qui me rend heureux'
Apprendre à célébrer sans déranger les autres
Respiration calme pour revenir au calme
closing.visualSupports: Cercle joyeux mais calme, démonstration de célébration appropriée

decisionPoints.situation: How do students show happiness appropriately?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students get too excited → teach 'joie calme' vs 'joie forte' | IF students reserved → encourage gentle expression

decisionPoints.situation: What activities bring students joy?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students love movement → more dancing activities | IF students prefer quiet → more art and bubbles

decisionPoints.situation: How to channel excitement positively?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF energy too high → more breathing breaks | IF energy good → maintain current level

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on simple 'content' vs 'très content'
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More bubbles, simpler activities
emergencyBackup.ifOverstimulated: Calmer activities, more breathing, less stimulation

lessons.realWorldConnection: Showing joy appropriately helps us share happiness with others without overwhelming them
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe appropriate joy expression, listen to joy vocabulary
lessons.differentiationSupport: Active learners: more movement | Quiet learners: art focus | Social: partner sharing

lessons.title: Quand je suis triste
lessons.goal: Students will learn healthy ways to cope with sadness and seek comfort
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 6 by exploring sadness and healthy coping strategies

activities: Rappel: 'On a exploré la joie'
Question douce: 'Parfois on se sent triste aussi'
Marionnette partage: 'Moi aussi je suis parfois triste'
Histoire: 'Emma se sent triste' - qu'est-ce qui aide?
Boîte de réconfort: découvrir objets qui consolent
Apprendre: 'Il est OK de pleurer'
Pratique: demander un câlin ou du réconfort
Création d'une carte de réconfort pour soi
mainActivity.visualSupports: Livre empathique, boîte douce, objets réconfortants, matériel d'art
mainActivity.movementBreak: Étirements doux et respirations calmantes

activities: Cercle de réconfort: 'Ce qui m'aide quand je suis triste'
Câlins de groupe optionnels
Chanson douce de réconfort
closing.visualSupports: Cercle chaleureux, peluches disponibles, ambiance apaisante

decisionPoints.situation: How comfortable are students with sadness?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students uncomfortable → more puppet examples, less personal | IF students open → gentle personal sharing OK

decisionPoints.situation: What comforting strategies work for this age?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students like touch → more hugs, soft items | IF students prefer space → more individual comfort items

decisionPoints.situation: How to normalize crying and seeking help?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF stigma around crying → more validation stories | IF students accepting → practice asking for help

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'triste' and 'câlin' with comfort items
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More comfort box exploration
emergencyBackup.ifTriggering: More puppet focus, less personal examples, more comfort available

lessons.realWorldConnection: When we're sad, asking for comfort helps us feel better and shows others how to help us
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe comfort-seeking behavior, listen to sadness vocabulary
lessons.differentiationSupport: Tactile learners: comfort items | Emotional: extra validation | Social: partner support

lessons.title: Quand je suis fâché
lessons.goal: Students will learn appropriate ways to express and manage anger
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 7 by focusing on anger management and healthy expression
safetyConsiderations: Enseigner expression sécuritaire de la colère

activities: Rappel: 'Tristesse, c'est normal'
Question: 'Qu'est-ce qui nous rend fâché parfois?'
Marionnette: 'Moi aussi je me fâche, mais je dois être sécuritaire'

mainActivity.description: Practice safe anger expression and calming
activities: Histoire: 'Alex est fâché' - que peut-il faire?
Démonstration: respirer profondément pour se calmer
Coussins de colère: frapper sécuritairement
Bouteille de calme: regarder jusqu'à être plus calme
Dessiner sa colère puis la transformer en calme
mainActivity.visualSupports: Livre, démonstrations claires, coussins sécuritaires, bouteille magique
mainActivity.movementBreak: Mouvements de boxe dans l'air (sans contact)

activities: Cercle: 'Une façon sécuritaire d'être fâché'
Pratique groupe: respirer ensemble pour se calmer
Plan: 'Quand je suis fâché, je peux...'
closing.visualSupports: Cercle sécuritaire, respiration guidée, affiche stratégies

decisionPoints.situation: How do students currently handle anger?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students hit/throw → more safe alternatives, more practice | IF students withdraw → validate and offer expression options

decisionPoints.situation: What calming strategies are age-appropriate?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF breathing works → add counting breaths | IF movement works → add safe movement options

decisionPoints.situation: How to address aggressive responses to anger?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF aggression present → clear boundaries, more safe alternatives | IF no aggression → reinforce current positive strategies

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'fâché' and breathing only
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More hands-on with cushions and bottles
emergencyBackup.ifTriggering: More puppet examples, immediate calming activities

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning to handle anger safely keeps us and others safe and helps solve problems
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe anger management attempts, listen to calming vocabulary
lessons.differentiationSupport: Kinesthetic: movement activities | Visual: calm bottle | Auditory: breathing counts

lessons.title: Quand j'ai peur
lessons.goal: Students will identify fears and learn strategies to feel brave and seek help
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 8 by exploring fear and developing courage and help-seeking
safetyConsiderations: Valider les peurs sans les minimiser
Enseigner quand demander de l'aide d'adulte
Éviter de créer plus de peurs

activities: Rappel: 'On peut gérer notre colère'
Question: 'Tout le monde a-t-il peur parfois?'
Marionnette: 'J'ai peur du noir, mais je peux être courageux'
Partage: 'Des peurs communes' (peur du noir, gros chiens, etc.)
Histoire: 'Marie a peur mais trouve du courage'
Lampe courage: allumer quand on a peur
Cape de courage: porter pour se sentir brave
Plan: 'Quand j'ai peur, je peux demander de l'aide à...'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Livre encourageant, lampe spéciale, cape amusante, photos inspirantes
mainActivity.movementBreak: Marche de courage - marcher comme un super-héros

activities: Cercle: 'Je suis courageux quand...'
Certificats de courage pour chacun
Promesse: 'Je peux demander de l'aide quand j'ai peur'
closing.visualSupports: Cercle supportant, certificats colorés, affiche des aides

decisionPoints.situation: What fears are common for this age group?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF common fears shared → normalize and address | IF unique fears → individual validation and strategies

decisionPoints.situation: How to address fears without dismissing them?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF fears seem 'silly' to others → validate all fears as real | IF fears are serious → ensure adult follow-up

decisionPoints.situation: What brave strategies can students use?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students like props → use more courage items | IF students prefer talk → more discussion strategies

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'peur' and 'demander aide' with simple examples
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More courage props and superhero play
emergencyBackup.ifTriggering: Less fear talk, more courage building and adult help focus

lessons.realWorldConnection: Being brave means we can try new things, and asking for help keeps us safe
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe courage building, listen to help-seeking language
lessons.differentiationSupport: Visual learners: courage props | Kinesthetic: superhero movements | Emotional: extra validation

lessons.title: Respirer pour me calmer
lessons.goal: Students will learn simple breathing exercises to self-regulate emotions
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 9 by introducing concrete self-regulation tools
safetyConsiderations: Respecter le confort respiratoire de chacun
Garder les exercices simples et courts

activities: Rappel: 'On peut être courageux et demander de l'aide'
Démonstration: respirer vite vs respirer lentement
Question: 'Comment se sent-on avec chaque respiration?'
Respiration plume: faire voler doucement avec l'expiration
Pinwheels: tourner lentement avec la respiration
Bulles calmes: respirer profondément pour faire de grosses bulles
Respiration animale: respirer comme un chien vs comme une tortue
Créer son propre 'outil respiration' (dessin ou craft)
mainActivity.visualSupports: Plumes colorées, pinwheels amusants, bulles magiques, livre animal
mainActivity.movementBreak: Yoga respiratoire simple (mains vers le ciel, respirer)

closing.description: Integrate breathing into daily emotional regulation
activities: Pratique groupe: respiration collective calme
Plan personnel: 'Quand utiliser ma respiration'
Respiration de fermeture: préparer pour la suite de la journée
closing.visualSupports: Groupe uni, respiration synchronisée, calme collectif

decisionPoints.situation: Which breathing techniques work best for 6-year-olds?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF plume technique works → add more prop breathing | IF props distracting → focus on simple in/out breathing

decisionPoints.situation: How to make breathing exercises engaging?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students love props → rotate through different tools | IF students prefer stories → add more animal breathing

decisionPoints.situation: Are students able to use breathing when upset?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students remember in calm → practice in slightly frustrated moments | IF students forget → more reminders and practice

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on simple 'in, out' breathing with counting
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More interactive props, less sitting still
emergencyBackup.ifOverstimulating: Simpler breathing, less props, more calm environment

lessons.realWorldConnection: Deep breathing helps us feel calmer anywhere - at home, school, or playing
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe breathing technique use, self-regulation attempts
lessons.differentiationSupport: Tactile learners: props focus | Visual: demonstration | Kinesthetic: movement breathing

lessons.title: Comprendre les autres
lessons.goal: Students will begin to recognize and respond to emotions in others
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 10 by extending emotional awareness to understanding others
safetyConsiderations: Respecter la vie privée des autres

activities: Rappel: 'On peut utiliser notre respiration pour se calmer'
Question: 'Comment savoir ce que ressentent nos amis?'
Marionnette regarde une autre: 'Je vois qu'elle est triste'

mainActivity.description: Practice reading and responding to others' emotions
activities: Photo mystère: 'Comment se sent cet enfant?' (avec indices)
Miroir empathie: copier l'expression d'un ami
Scénarios: 'Si ton ami pleure, tu peux...'
Jeu gentillesse: donner un cœur à quelqu'un qui en a besoin
Histoire: 'Thomas aide sa sœur qui est fâchée'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Photos expressives, miroirs, cartes scénarios, cœurs colorés
mainActivity.movementBreak: Marcher et offrir des sourires aux amis

activities: Cercle: 'Comment j'ai aidé quelqu'un aujourd'hui'
Création affiche: 'Façons d'être gentil'
Promesse: 'Je vais regarder comment se sentent mes amis'
closing.visualSupports: Cercle empathique, affiche collaborative, engagement positif

decisionPoints.situation: How well can students read others' emotions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students struggle → use more obvious expressions, more modeling | IF students good → add subtle emotions

decisionPoints.situation: What empathy skills are developmentally appropriate?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students show natural empathy → encourage with specific strategies | IF empathy challenging → model extensively

decisionPoints.situation: How to encourage kind responses to others' feelings?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students want to help → teach appropriate help | IF students avoid → model gentle approaches

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'ami triste' and 'être gentil'
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More mirror play and heart giving

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding others helps us be better friends and makes everyone feel good
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe empathy attempts, listen to other-focused language
lessons.differentiationSupport: Social learners: partner work | Visual: photo focus | Emotional: extra empathy modeling

lessons.title: Aider un ami triste
lessons.goal: Students will learn how to comfort and support friends who are upset
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 11 by practicing specific empathy and helping skills
safetyConsiderations: Respecter quand quelqu'un veut être seul

activities: Rappel: 'On peut comprendre comment se sentent nos amis'
Question: 'Que faire quand un ami est triste?'
Marionnettes: une console l'autre qui pleure
Boîte à outils: découvrir façons d'aider (écouter, câlin, chercher adulte)
Role-play marionnettes: 'Mon ami est tombé et pleure'
Pratique: dire 'Ça va aller' et 'Je peux t'aider'
Histoire: 'Sarah aide Ben qui a peur'
Création carte de réconfort pour un ami
mainActivity.visualSupports: Boîte interactive, marionnettes, livre consolant, matériel d'art
mainActivity.movementBreak: Pratique: offrir un câlin respectueux

activities: Cercle: 'Comment je peux aider un ami triste'
Certificats d'ami aidant pour chacun
Plan: 'Quand demander l'aide d'un grand'
closing.visualSupports: Cercle supportant, certificats fiers, plan d'action clair

decisionPoints.situation: What helping strategies are appropriate for this age?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students want to fix problems → teach listening and presence | IF students avoid helping → model simple approaches

decisionPoints.situation: How to teach helping without fixing?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students try to solve everything → teach 'être là' for friend | IF students just watch → encourage simple actions

decisionPoints.situation: When should students get adult help?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF situation serious → clear adult rules | IF minor upset → teach student helping first

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 'ami triste' and 'dire à madame'
emergencyBackup.ifNotEngaged: More puppet demonstrations and hands-on practice
emergencyBackup.ifOverwhelming: Simpler helping: just 'tu vas bien?' and get adult

lessons.realWorldConnection: Helping sad friends makes them feel better and makes us good friends
lessons.assessmentOpportunities: Observe helping attempts, listen to supportive language
lessons.differentiationSupport: Social learners: role-play focus | Emotional: extra modeling | Practical: concrete helping tools

lessons.title: Mes stratégies émotionnelles
lessons.goal: Students will identify their personal toolkit of strategies for managing different emotions
lessons.connectionToPrevious: Builds on Lesson 12 by creating personalized emotional regulation toolkits

opening.description: Review learning journey and introduce toolkit concept
activities: Rappel: 'On a appris tellement sur les émotions!'
Question: 'Quels outils avons-nous pour nos émotions?'
Présentation: 'Chacun aura sa boîte spéciale d'outils'
Révision outils: respiration, câlins, aide, etc.
Choisir ses 3 stratégies préférées
Décorer sa boîte personnelle d'outils émotionnels
Créer cartes-rappel avec dessins
Test: 'Quand je suis triste, j'utilise...'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Cartes stratégies, boîtes colorées, photos-rappel, matériel créatif
mainActivity.movementBreak: Pratique rapide: utiliser une stratégie choisie

activities: Présentation: montrer sa boîte et ses outils préférés
Promesse: 'J'utiliserai mes outils quand j'en ai besoin'
Placement spécial des boîtes dans la classe
closing.visualSupports: Présentation fière, engagement personnel, espace classe

decisionPoints.situation: Which strategies work best for each student?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF student prefers movement → include movement strategies | IF student prefers quiet → include calm strategies

decisionPoints.situation: How to personalize emotional regulation tools?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF student has clear preferences → honor and build on them | IF student unsure → guide with gentle suggestions

decisionPoints.situation: Are students able to choose appropriate strategies?
decisionPoints.ifThen: IF students choose well → celebrate and confirm | IF choices don't match → gentle guidance and discussion

emergencyBackup.ifTooAdvanced: Focus on 2 simple strategies only
